niche_preference_profile: This user most consistently prefers interfaces with strong, clear hierarchy; compact but organized layouts when density improves utility; cleaner and simpler compositions with reduced decorative clutter; grouped, card-based structure that makes sections easy to scan; moderate rather than exaggerated rounding; darker or more muted backgrounds when they improve focus, though they also accept light neutral themes when restrained; and selective use of vivid accents or imagery when they create emphasis, clarity, or product visibility rather than noise.

top_7_criteria.description: Prefers interfaces with strong emphasis, obvious sectioning, bold headlines or dominant primary areas, and clearer differentiation between primary and secondary content.
Prefers content grouped into clearly separated sections, unified cards, aligned lists, or structured containers rather than mixed, fragmented, or dispersed layouts.
Prefers fewer decorative elements, less visual clutter, concise copy, and restrained presentation over busy, noisy, or overly embellished screens.
Usually prefers compact, information-dense layouts that expose more useful content at once, especially in utility workflows, though not when density harms hierarchy or form clarity.
Prefers moderately rounded cards, dialogs, and softened surfaces, avoiding both overly exaggerated pill-like rounding and overly rigid boxed segmentation.
Prefers backgrounds and elevation treatments that create focus on the main content, such as dimmed backdrops, darker surrounding surfaces, floating modals, and subtle shadows.
Prefers vivid accents, strong CTA contrast, visible imagery, and highlighted product or media content when they improve emphasis, recognizability, or engagement without adding clutter.
